correctness.rationale: Ito–Zeng–Zeng use classical (thick) generation by all integral tensor powers; their proper-toric criterion applies to this smooth complete complex fan. The anticanonical polytope is full-dimensional because the origin is strictly inside all defining half-spaces, and bounded by completeness. Thus X itself passes the big/anti-big criterion; points do also. Adjunction on each invariant P¹ gives anticanonical degree 2+D_i², so the remaining obstruction is exactly an invariant (−2)-curve. For the gap, the standard minimal-model list reduces seven rays to four star subdivisions of the projective-plane fan or three of a Hirzebruch fan. A separate geometric replay used v_i+v_{i+1} at every cyclic edge and computed each self-intersection as −det(v_{i−1},v_{i+1}). All 360 plane histories give (−2), with 13 dihedral strings. All 120 Hirzebruch histories give a constant (−2) entry, with 21 formal strings: in the starting fan (1,0),(0,1),(−1,n),(0,−1) only y coordinates depend on n, which remains true after subdivisions and makes every determinant affine; evaluation at n=0 and 1 recovers its constant and slope exactly. Thus there is no cutoff in n in this replay. The small fans have strings (1,1,1), (0,0,0,0), (0,−1,−1,−1,0) up to rotation, and all −1 at six rays. The specified eight- and nine-ray strings were independently recovered, respectively (−3,−1,−3,−1,−3,−4,0,3) and (−3,−1,−3,−1,−4,−1,−5,0,3). For each, the stated two-edge operation preserves a triple with central −1 and both neighbors ≤−3, proving the infinite tail by induction, not by finite iterations. The toric divisor sequence gives ρ=r−2; Noether's formula uses χ(O_X)=1 and e(X)=r, giving K²=12−r.
residual_risks: This uses the standard classification into toric blowups of P² or Hirzebruch fans. The existence spectrum does not enumerate all qualifying fans at each attainable r.
